meta.name: HAX presentations
meta.about: Talks, podcasts and webinars about HAX. Portals (shared ids) link back to hax-ecosystem.json for details.

t17balt.desc: DrupalCon Baltimore. The ELMS:LN core team on web components, Polymer and "what HAX is (and how far along we are with it)." The first HAX talk.

t18nash.desc: DrupalCon Nashville: decoupling authoring for Drupal and beyond. "This isn't tied to Drupal; we've integrated it into Drupal which means it can integrate anywhere else easily."

t18gov.desc: Drupal GovCon 2018, in the DC area.
t18gov.yearNote: HAX: the best Drupal authoring experience, by not making it for Drupal

t19seattle.desc: Co-presented web components with Red Hat and announced HAXcms with an early prototype.

t19gov.yearNote: Future proofing design work with web components

t19apereo.desc: HAX and HAXcms for the Apereo higher-education open source community.

t23njcamp.yearNote: HAX: decoupling authoring from Drupal to use anywhere

t23ontology.desc: The course model under every instructional feature: outcomes, pedagogy, structure, instruction, content and assessment. "It doesn't need to be ideal. It does need to be valid."

t23horizon.desc: Where HAX was and where it said it would go: every site is a site.json plus static HTML. "When we blow up the notion of a database… we can build anything."

t24hitech.desc: The origin story in Bryan's words, with instructional designers reacting live. "I don't want humanity to need to code in order to put themselves on the internet."
t24hitech.yearNote: HiTech Podcast ep. 168: Reclaiming the Internet

t24fossy.desc: A conference talk introducing HAX: "My social cause: reduce the cost of web publishing to zero, regardless of ability."

t25state.desc: Year one of HAX Lab, the seven community pillars and the 2025 roadmap. "Meet our users where they are, not where we wish them to be."

t25fossy.desc: HAX Lab, a student club, a security reporting pipeline, the HAX CLI and ten years of history.
t25fossy.yearNote: FOSSY 2025: ten years from a notepad

t25wilson.desc: An interview by Apereo Board Chair Joshua Wilson on Bryan's model for community building: a 200-level class that uses HAX, a weekly HAX Club, then paid HAX Lab internships, with college grants and the CLI letting agents build sites.

t26nothing.desc: Ten years of HAX through ubiquity, the outline designer and SIIP; why every site since 2020 still works.
t26nothing.yearNote: Nothing is intentional, until it is

t26siip.desc: The pipeline, told by the students and faculty in it, with live demos of skeletons, Pressbooks import and Canvas AI analysis.

t26tools.desc: The talk Bryan ends his courses with: his career as one storyline, the retirement of the EdTechJoker persona, and the family saying in its title. Automation begets automation, from a 2015 bash-script keynote to AI in 2026.
t26tools.yearNote: With the right tools, you can do anything

tmanymes.desc: A workshop for instructional and learning design staff: build a digital "you" from context, skills, inputs, rules and outputs. PRAW is the worked example.

tperf.desc: Offline-capable sites with high performance scores while shipping unbundled ES modules.

source.label: WINS.md: Fast without a build step

tminute.desc: HAX explained in under a minute, the short intro linked from the Apereo project page.

tgov4.desc: A Drupal4Gov webinar series session on HAX.

govcon.desc: A Drupal conference in the Washington, DC area.

drupalcampnj.desc: A regional Drupal camp in New Jersey.

fossy.desc: Free and Open Source Software Yearly, run by Software Freedom Conservancy.

hitech.desc: A podcast hosted by instructional designers Josh Schwartz and Will Illingworth.

drupal4gov.desc: A webinar series for Drupal in government.

tours.label: The story in talks
tours.message: Ten years of HAX told through the talks that introduced it, from the ELMS:LN core team at DrupalCon to the SIIP conversation at Apereo.

scenes.caption: Every talk hangs off one hub.
2017: the ELMS:LN core team shows HAX for the first time at DrupalCon Baltimore.
2018: Nashville and Drupal GovCon take HAX beyond Drupal.
2019: HAXcms is announced in Seattle; Apereo and GovCon follow.
2023: the course ontology, the Horizon Report and DrupalCamp NJ.
2024: the origin story on a podcast, and the revolution at FOSSY.
2025: the State of HAX Community names the seven pillars; FOSSY gets ten years in one talk.
Late 2025: Apereo's board chair asks how the class, the club and the lab fit together.
2026: Nothing is intentional, until it is; then SIIP at Apereo with the students and faculty themselves.
And the talk that ends every course: with the right tools, you can do anything.
Still to date: workshops and videos that need a year.
Every talk points back into the ecosystem web.
